result.summary: The intersection is equipped with essential pedestrian infrastructure, including high-visibility zebra crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and ADA-compliant curb ramps with tactile warning pads. However, the environment lacks advanced traffic calming features like curb extensions, and a large evergreen tree on the corner creates a significant visual obstruction for sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Vegetation
hazards.description: A large evergreen tree on the corner significantly blocks the line of sight between pedestrians waiting to cross and drivers approaching the intersection from the side street.
hazards.location_in_image: Far right corner of the intersection, adjacent to the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Wide Curb Radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry allows for relatively high-speed right turns, increasing the risk of collisions with pedestrians in the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: The corner where the white vehicle is positioned.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and force drivers to take turns at slower, safer speeds.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Trim or relocate the large evergreen tree to ensure clear sightlines for all road users at the intersection.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a clearly marked zebra crosswalk and a wide, unobstructed sidewalk adjacent to commercial buildings. Safety is compromised by the lack of active traffic control and parked vehicles that obstruct sightlines at the crossing point.

hazards.name: Parked vehicles near crosswalk
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the crosswalk markings obstruct the visibility between pedestrians and oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway, adjacent to the crosswalk

hazards.name: Lack of traffic control
hazards.description: The crossing is marked but lacks stop signs, traffic signals, or pedestrian-activated beacons to manage vehicle flow.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and prevent parking too close to the crosswalk, improving visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for both drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-activated flashing lights to increase driver yielding rates at this uncontrolled crossing.

result.summary: The intersection features basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked crosswalks, sidewalks, and traffic signals. However, the wide roadway and lack of physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions increase pedestrian exposure to turning vehicles.

hazards.name: Wide Turning Radii
hazards.description: The wide corners allow vehicles to maintain higher speeds while turning through the pedestrian crosswalks.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection corners near the crosswalk entrances.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Visible cracking and uneven patching in the roadway near the crosswalks may create tripping hazards or affect vehicle control.
hazards.location_in_image: In the foreground and center of the intersection roadway.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Constructing curb extensions would shorten the crossing distance for pedestrians and force drivers to slow down when making turns.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to provide pedestrians with a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic receives a green light.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Refresh the existing markings with high-visibility continental patterns to improve driver awareness of the crossing zone.

result.summary: The intersection features a marked continental crosswalk and ADA-compliant curb ramps with tactile warnings. However, the wide roadway and lack of visible pedestrian signals or refuge islands increase exposure for people crossing.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to cross multiple lanes without a median or refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main road

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible to indicate safe crossing intervals at this signalized intersection.

hazards.name: Pavement degradation
hazards.description: Cracking and patching in the roadway surface near the crosswalk could present tripping hazards or affect vehicle braking.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to clarify crossing phases.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and increase the visibility of pedestrians to approaching drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Refresh
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-durability materials to ensure maximum visibility.
